head: claude/decision-answers-guard
title: fix(decisions): make a written operator answer READABLE by the grader (+ guard)
body:
## What

Two decision requests carried an operator answer **the grader could not see**, so the inbox kept listing them and the sweep kept re-prompting the operator with options they had already refused.

`grade_answer_state()` reads `request["answer"]` and nothing else, and `normalise_answer()` returns `None` unless that block holds a non-empty `chosen` or `free_text`. Every other key — however much reasoning it carries — is invisible to it.

| request | what was wrong | now |
|---|---|---|
| `DEC-20260904-DEMOTE-AND-TUNE-FLOW` | answer recorded at object level | nested, grades `committed` |
| `DEC-20260902-LOCAL-LLM-WEIGHT` | rich block with `chosen: null`, no `free_text` | `chosen` + `free_text` added, grades `committed` |

**The second is why the operator was asked the same question repeatedly.** They answered on 2026-09-02; the block was written the same day and graded `not_submitted`, so they were re-asked on 09-04. Measured by running the real normaliser over the file, not by inspection: `normalise_answer() -> None`.

Its answer refuses **all three** declared options — neither size arm is adopted **and** the path is not shelved — which is precisely what the option set could not express between them. The operator's directive to file a ROADMAP milestone for a *production-ready* LLM is recorded as **still owed**, explicitly not as filed.

## The guard is the point, not the two fixes

This is the **second instance of one class in a single day**, and both were found by hand. A reminder to "remember to fill in `chosen`" is the non-mechanism this repo has already paid for twice (MI-15, `BL-20260903-MANAGER-CHECKLIST-GOES-STALE-SILENTLY`), so `scripts/ci/check_decision_answers.py` checks two shapes:

- **R1** — an in-request `answer:` block that `normalise_answer()` cannot read.
- **R2** — an answer filed only at OBJECT level, where the grader never looks.

Registered **ungated** in `run_guards.py`: the failure is a decision object going quiet, which a diff-scoped guard cannot see regress when an unrelated PR edits the row. The tree was **measured clean first** — 614 objects, 0 unparseable, 0 findings — so nothing is grandfathered and there is no separate standing audit for anyone to forget to run.

## Verification

- Self-test: **7 cases**, run on every invocation. On a clean tree this guard is otherwise only ever observed *passing*, which is the state a guard is least useful in.
- **Replayed against the two pre-fix files at `HEAD`** to prove it catches the real instances, not only its own fixtures: the LOCAL-LLM object produced 2 findings.
- **R2 was tightened after that replay.** It fired on the SUNSET object's *correct* shape — one request answered-and-nested, a second genuinely open, plus a historical top-level block recording the first. It now fires only when no request on the object carries a readable nested answer, and that false-positive shape is one of the seven self-test cases. A guard that fires on the correct state is how a guard gets ignored.

## What this does NOT check

It cannot tell whether an answer is the *right* one, nor whether the free text says what the operator meant. It checks exactly one thing: that a block a human wrote as an answer will be **read** as one.

## Tier

Tier-1, self-landing (`.github/pr-landing/decision-answers-guard.json`). All paths are `scripts/ci/**` and `docs/claude/work/objects/**`. No runtime, order path, strategy config, risk cap, deploy file or live-VM file is touched; the guard reads YAML and exits non-zero — it enacts nothing.
